chapter: Early New Orleans bands and records
title: Monk Hazel and the Bienville Roof
summary: Playing a season on the Bienville Roof with Monk Hazel, who recorded with Sharkey directing, and Charlie Wagner.

bands.name: Monk Hazel and his Bienville Roof Orchestra

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. Yeah. Well I was going to ask about the one, one of your earliest records is the one called Monk Hazel and his Bienville Roof Orchestra under the leadership or under direction of Sharkey, Bonanno it was called.
Did you play there with Monk on the Bienville Roof for a while?

Yes, I played with Monk on the Bienville Roof. We had, in fact we had two trumpets on the roof but we only had one trumpet when we made the record. Yeah. The other trumpet player, his name was Charlie Wagner.
Oh I've heard of him, he was out in Metry, he died just a year or two ago.
That was when we were playing on the Bienville Roof. Now when we made the record... It was down by Lee Circle? Yes, that's an office building now.
Yeah, it's an office building, I never knew from how it was a hotel.
That was a nice hotel. Yeah. They had a nice roof up there. Yeah. Roof up there, yeah.
I never got the seat up. Yeah.
And Monk had a fine band. They had a real good band. In fact we made some real good records there at that time.
Yeah, in high society. That was a wonderful session. That was a wonderful session. Sizzling, yes, and that's a very good record. And did you work there long with him or...?
Yes, we worked there a whole season. Whole season. Mm-hmm. Well in fact it was one of the outstanding places at that time.

Yeah, it must have been. See, like the Blue Room is today, well that was the Bienville Roof. I remember I heard you at the Blue Room in 1938 when I, one of the first times I came to town. Here, after I heard you in New York. You were back, where didn't the Blue Room? Yeah, no, the Fontaine Lounge. Oh yeah, maybe that's where it was, yeah. At least the Rocheville Hotel. Yeah, that's right. The Fontaine Lounge, yeah. I was going to ask about another early record you made back in the 20's with Johnny Miller. And Sidney Aroden is on there. That's right. Plays the Bindler. Yeah. Dipper Mouth and Panama. Dipper Mouth, Panama. I think you made some other tunes. They only brought out the one record I believe though. Is that right? I think so, just those two sides. I believe, Panama and Dipper Mouth.
